C.2 New York Independent System Operator AC Transmission Needs The PPTPP is a joint planning process conducted by the NYISO and NYPSC as part of the NYISO’s Comprehensive System Planning Process (NYISO, n.d.-a). The process represents an innovative partnership between the ISO and regulator, establishing a role for the NYPSC to identify transmission needs and cost allocation solutions for projects to meet public policy requirements. The PPTPP starts with the NYISO identifying and submitting transmission needs to NYPSC for consideration to be included as a public policy transmission need. After approval from NYPSC, the NYISO then solicits input from developers and stakeholders to identify and evaluate transmission solutions to meet the public policy transmission need. 57 This report is available at no cost from the National Laboratory of the Rockies at www.nlr.gov/publications. The AC Transmission Needs project was initiated through an order from NYPSC in December 2015 identifying a public policy need to increase transfer capacity along two corridors from upstate to downstate New York (Proceeding on Motion of the Commission To Examine Alternating Current Transmission Upgrades 2015). The identified need followed a State Transmission Assessment and Reliability Study (NYISO Board of Directors 2019) led by the NYISO and Energy Highway Blueprint released by Governor Andrew Cuomo (New York Energy Highway Task Force 2012). The order required no less than 350 megawatts (MW) of transfer capability for Segment A and 900-MW transfer capability for Segment B. The NYISO issued a solicitation for solutions to meet this need in February 2016 followed by an order from the NYPSC in January 2017 affirming the NYISO’s determination of AC Transmission Needs and directing the NYISO to evaluate and select transmission solutions to meet this need. The PPTPP allows for flexibility in designing the scenarios and sensitivities used for project evaluation based on the project context and stakeholder input. It also authorizes the NYPSC to identify additional benefit criteria—both quantitative and qualitative—and the NYISO Board to select projects based on multivalue criteria rather than solely on project cost.17 The selected solutions consist of upgrades to existing lines from 230 kV to 345 kV between central and east New York (Segment A) and replacing 115-kV and 69-kV lines with new double- circuit 345-kV lines between Albany and downstate New York (Segment B) (NYISO 2019c). The proposed solutions for both segments had higher costs than alternatives but were selected based on the projects’ benefits including increased transfer capacity, deferred transmission upgrades, greater operational flexibility, and more resilient structure design.
